title: De lineis curvis non in eodem plano sitis, quae maximi minimive proprietate sunt praeditae

deep.reconstruction:
Problem V asks for the space curve that makes the integral of w(v) ds stationary, where v = |r| = sqrt(x²+y²+z²) and w is an arbitrary function of v. In modern terms this is a geodesic of the conformally flat, spherically symmetric metric w(|r|)²|dr|². Equivalently it is a light ray in a radially stratified medium (Fermat's principle). It is also a trajectory under a central force via the Maupertuis–Jacobi principle, taking w = sqrt(E − U(v)).

§31. Euler writes dy = p dx and dz = q dx with s = sqrt(1+p²+q²), so the integrand is V(x,y,z,p,q) = w s. Using dw = w' dv, dv = (x dx + y dy + z dz)/v and ds = (p dp + q dq)/s, he reads off the partial derivatives in his usual notation:
- M = V_x = w' s x / v
- N = V_y = w' s y / v
- N' = V_z = w' s z / v
- P = V_p = w p / s
- P' = V_q = w q / s
He then forms S = V − pP − qP' = w(s² − p² − q²)/s = w/s.

§32. The three conditions are:
- I. M dx = dS, i.e. (w' s x/v) dx = d(w/s). This is the 'x-equation' or Beltrami-type identity; it is a consequence of the other two, since dS = M dx + p(N dx − dP) + q(N' dx − dP').
- II. N dx = dP, the Euler–Lagrange equation in y.
- III. N' dx = dP', the Euler–Lagrange equation in z.
Expand d(wp/s) = w dp/s + p d(w/s), and likewise for q. Replacing d(w/s) by its value from I eliminates it and gives:
- (w's/v)(y dx − x dy) = w dp/s
- (w's/v)(z dx − x dz) = w dq/s
Dividing by v these become (y dx − x dy)/v² = w dp/(w' v s²) and (z dx − x dz)/v² = w dq/(w' v s²).

Purpose (completed on the next page): dividing one equation by the other gives d(z − qx)/(z − qx) = d(y − px)/(y − px). Integrating yields z = my + nx, so the extremal lies in a plane through the centre (the analogue of angular-momentum conservation). The problem then reduces to a separated planar equation in u = y/x and p.
errors: Equation I is printed (as far as the scan shows) as w'sx∂x/s = ∂(w/s). By the definition M = w'sx/v it should be w'sx∂x/v = ∂(w/s).
The value substituted for ∂(w/s) is printed as w'sx∂x/w; it should be w'sx∂x/v. The subsequent equations are correct, which confirms the denominator v was intended.
No substantive mathematical error. Euler also does not remark that equation I is dependent on II and III, but he uses it only as an auxiliary.

ideas.what: Variational problem ∫ w(|r|) ds for space curves, with integrand V = w s and the auxiliary quantity S = V − pP − qP' = w/s
ideas.modern_name: Geodesics of a conformally flat, radially symmetric metric; Fermat's principle in a spherically symmetric medium; Jacobi metric for central forces
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum II, for the planar central-force case; E740 itself for the space-curve version

ideas.what: Using the x-equation M dx = dS to eliminate d(w/s) and obtain the forms y dx − x dy and z dx − x dz, which are components of r × dr
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange equations plus the Erdmann/Beltrami-type identity; angular-momentum (Noether) structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Methodus 1744; general rule for three coordinates); Noether for the symmetry interpretation

ideas.what: Planarity of the extremal through the centre, deduced by integrating the ratio of the two equations (on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Conservation of the direction of angular momentum, giving planar orbits under central forces
ideas.where_published: Standard in Euler's mechanics (Mechanica 1736) for central forces

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine application of Euler's established three-coordinate variational method to a radially symmetric integrand. The resulting planarity is classical (central-force orbits), and the page contains only careful but standard elimination steps plus minor typographical slips.
transcription_corrections: Equation I: the denominator printed as 's' should be 'v' (w'sx∂x/v = ∂.w/s); the transcription reproduces the misprint.
'scribatur ejus valor ex I. aequatione w'sx∂x/w' should read w'sx∂x/v.
On the next page, the ratio should be (z∂x − x∂z)/(y∂x − x∂y) = ∂q/∂p, not ∂y/∂p.
On the previous page, 'coordinanatas' is a printer's/hyphenation duplication of 'coordinatas'.
